title: Correlated Code Vulnerabilities: Do Models Insert the Same Insecure Patterns?

original_idea.body:
# Correlated Code Vulnerabilities: Do Models Insert the Same Insecure Patterns?

**Problem:** Success state: organizations using AI coding assistants know whether switching models actually changes their vulnerability exposure.

**Direction:** Use a public set of security-sensitive coding prompts. Generate completions from several open code-capable models and run a static analyzer for known vulnerability classes. Measure whether the SAME vulnerabilities appear across models.

**Why it matters:** If every model plants the same vulnerability, an attacker who knows the shared blind spot can exploit code generated everywhere simultaneously.

**Relevant context:** Combines Artificial Hivemind homogeneity with secure-code benchmarks.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong, concrete chain: shared insecure code idioms across models enable mass exploitation, a defensible high-impact scenario.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Public insecure-code benchmarks + off-the-shelf static analyzers; accessible to beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: generate completions, run static analysis, measure cross-model correlation.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open code models + open analyzers, independent-friendly, weak lab incentive.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference + static analysis on a single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Insecure-code generation is studied; the cross-model correlation angle may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Insecure-code generation is studied; the cross-model correlation angle may be open.
